clue.text: Charm is not working for the royal family

indicators.note: something not working is out of order, so these letters must be put into a new order

explanation.surface: A lucky charm has failed to work for the Windsors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' looks like part of the indicator but it is fodder; 'working' is the indicator, rearranging CHARMISNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of monarchy is in favour of keeping a royal house on the throne.

clue.text: Fruits said to cause disease

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read as written

parts.note: two fruits, each a berry, give the two halves of the sound

explanation.surface: Some fruits are claimed to make people ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a deficiency disease caused by lack of vitamin B1, so it is one illness by name.

arson, the deliberate setting of fires, is a crime

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes a lenient line on criminal behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so P sits on top of ARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman of a parish is a minister of the church, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: A 16 can be lethal

parts.note: the answer to 16 across, the former Conservative leader, is known by his initials I D S

explanation.surface: A certain politician is a deadly danger.
explanation.walkthrough: '16' points to the 16-across answer, the Tory leader commonly called IDS after his initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The disease caused by the HIV virus may prove fatal, so the description identifies it loosely.

clue.text: Annual pest can be disagreeable

indicators.note: can be suggests these letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A yearly garden pest may be a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nasty or unpleasing is disagreeable, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Vehicles boy goes in are always late

indicators.note: goes in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: cars are vehicles
Dave is a boy's name

explanation.surface: The cars a lad rides in never turn up on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' is the trick: it means dead, not tardy, and a corpse is dead for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpses are the dead, and 'late' means deceased, so they are permanently in that state.

clue.text: Where a lot of money is lost, but turns up on one's account

explanation.surface: A gambling den where cash vanishes, though some reappears in one's bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses ON + IS + AC together, giving the answer read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling house is a place where punters lose large sums at the tables.

clue.text: Admiral finished as next to no good

indicators.note: next to means the two pieces are set side by side

parts.note: by can mean over or past, as in 'the time is by'

explanation.surface: An admiral came to a bad end as he was useless.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral John Byng was executed in 1757 for failing to relieve Minorca, which gives the surface its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: John Byng was a British admiral, famously shot on his own quarterdeck in 1757.

clue.text: Frank keeps proportion in theatrical performance

indicators.note: keeps means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: frank means open, candid
a ratio is a proportion

explanation.surface: A candid actor maintains balance during a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatrical' is a pun: surgery happens in an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery takes place in an operating theatre, so a surgical procedure is jokingly a theatre performance.

clue.text: Lack of control in a Hackney report

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a Hackney carriage is a London taxi, so the phrase gives 'a taxi'

explanation.surface: A loss of control is mentioned in a London cab driver's account.
explanation.walkthrough: A Hackney carriage is the formal name for a London black cab; Hackney is also a London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Ataxy, more often ataxia, is loss of muscular coordination, so the body is out of control.

clue.text: Macdonalds, perhaps, put ecstasy in char

explanation.definitionFit: To char is to do housework as a cleaning lady, so it means to clean.

clue.text: College support sees no uncertainty

parts.note: a bra is a support garment

explanation.walkthrough: 'uncertainty' rearranges SEESNO into SENOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasenose is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: A dart aimed at the bull

definitions.text: A dart aimed at the bull

parts.words: A dart aimed at the bull
parts.note: reads like a darts player going for the bullseye, but describes the barbed stick plunged into a bull in the ring

explanation.definitionFit: In bullfighting a decorated barbed dart is thrust into the neck of the bull.

clue.text: Cheer at Sussex town centre — at a price

indicators.note: centre means only the middle of the town's name is kept, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: Bexhill is a seaside town in East Sussex, England
a rate is a price, as in a going rate

explanation.walkthrough: Bexhill-on-Sea is a resort on the south coast of England; 'centre' trims its first and last letters to EXHIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhilarate someone is to elate or enliven them, which is to cheer them.

clue.text: Indians ain't much moved by old chief with muted war cry

definitions.text: old chief with muted war cry

indicators.note: moved means the letters are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: Native Americans are unimpressed by an elderly chief whose battle cry is subdued.
explanation.walkthrough: The Conservative leader called himself 'the quiet man', hence the muted war cry; 'moved' rearranges INDIANSAINTMUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the Conservative Party from 2001 to 2003 and styled himself 'the quiet man'.

clue.text: Reject a girl who's not Rosy?

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
sallow describes a sickly yellowish complexion, the opposite of rosy

explanation.surface: Turn down a girl who isn't called Rosy?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosy' is capitalised to pass as a name, but it describes a complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: To disallow a claim or goal is to reject it as invalid.

clue.text: Pump for Latin translation

indicators.note: translation turns words into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pump is needed for translating Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that blows up tyres or balloons is a pump.

clue.text: Passing trains on network

indicators.note: on in the sense of running or under way, prompting a rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: a net is a network

explanation.surface: Trains go past on the rail network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' rearranges TRAINS with NET.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transient is fleeting, passing quickly away.

clue.text: It describes how 3 turns up in bad form

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other
form means the letters are shaped into a new arrangement
in a down clue turns up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the answer to 3 down is a minister, and Rev is a minister's title

explanation.surface: A clergyman turns up behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference '3' is the minister of 3-down, and 'Rev' is the title of any clergyman; 'form' rearranges 'bad' into ADB around the upturned title.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb modifies a verb, typically telling how something is done.

clue.text: A bus broken down on the way is ridiculous

indicators.note: broken down means the letters have fallen apart into a new order

parts.note: rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A bus that breaks down en route is laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken down' turns BUS into BSU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurd is ridiculous, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Seasonal listening for one awaiting a connection?

definitions.text: Seasonal listening for one awaiting a connection?

parts.words: Seasonal listening for one awaiting a connection?

clue.text: In place of five diamonds

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Instead of five gems.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin preposition means instead of, as in vice-captain standing in for the captain.

clue.text: Feeling of boy getting two ducks?

parts.note: Des is a boy's name, short for Desmond
in cricket a pair is two ducks, out for nought in both innings

explanation.surface: How a lad feels after scoring nought twice?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, and a pair is a duck in both innings of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopelessness is a feeling, and the answer names that emotion.

clue.text: Odd not to get the Guardian, which is a collector's item

explanation.walkthrough: Guardian setters use 'the Guardian' for US, as the paper speaking of itself.

clue.text: One may get drunk on ale glut or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so these letters are rearranged
